items.fullText: 경제 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 400억 쏟았는데 가동도 못 한다…경남 '풍력 시험장' 어쩌나 입력 2026.11.07 17:06 수정 2026.11.07 17:06 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 신현보 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 설계변경에 42억원 추가 투입 환율·건축비 92억원 확보도 못 해 경남도의회 “정상가동 방안 시급” 사진은 기사 내용과 무관. /사진=게티이미지뱅크 400억원을 들여 추진한 국내 첫 풍력 너셀 시험시설이 당초 계획보다 2년 늦어졌지만, 추가 예산마저 확보하지 못해 정상 운영 시점을 장담하기 어려운 상황에 놓였다. 7일 경남도의회에 따르면 경제환경위원회는 전날 경남도 산업국 행정사무감사에서 창원 가포신항 배후부지에 조성 중인 풍력 너셀 테스트베드 사업의 지연 문제를 집중적으로 따졌다. 이 사업은 풍력발전기의 핵심 장비인 너셀의 성능을 시험·검증할 시설을 만드는 프로젝트다. 정부와 경남도, 창원시가 2020년부터 경남테크노파크를 수행기관으로 정해 국비와 지방비 400억원을 투입했다. 당초 2024년 완공을 목표로 했지만 매립지 특성에 따른 설계변경이 발생하면서 42억원이 더 들어갔고, 사업기간도 올해 말까지 연장됐다. 문제는 추가 비용이 여기서 끝나지 않았다는 점이다. 유로화 환율 변동에 따른 29억원과 독일산 시험장비 설치 등에 필요한 건축비 63억원도 아직 마련되지 않았다. 기존 사업비를 포함하면 추가 부담이 100억원을 훌쩍 넘어선 셈이다. 도의회는 이미 수백억원이 투입된 만큼 책임 공방보다 시설을 실제 가동할 수 있는 대책이 우선이라고 주문했다. 김구연 경제환경위원장은 “지금까지 사업을 추진하면서 발생한 잘못을 확인하고 책임을 짚는 것도 필요하지만, 이제는 대규모 예산을 투입한 시설을 어떻게 정상 가동할 것인지 방안을 마련하는 일이 시급하다”고 강조했다. 강민승 의원은 “매립지에 시설을 건립하는 사업인데도 경남테크노파크가 토목 담당 직원이 없는 상황에서 바닷물 유입 가능성과 지반 보강 필요성, 공법 변경 및 추가 공사비의 적정성을 충분히 검토했는지 의문”이라고 지적했다. 정규헌 의원도 “도가 2024년 사업비 증가 필요성을 인지하고도 2년이 지난 현재까지 부족한 재원을 확보하지 못했다”며 “수백억 원을 투입한 시설이 정상 가동되지 못한다는 사실이 도저히 이해되지 않는다”고 비판했다. 신현보 한경닷컴 기자 greaterfool@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 신현보 기자 국회 출입 기자. 숫자와 현장을 바탕으로 우리 사회 문제를 추적합니다. (사진=농림축산식품부) 정부가 재생에너지 공급의무화제도(RPS) 개편에 맞춰 영농형태양광과 햇빛소득마을에 별도 발전수익 우대 혜택을 부여하는 방안을 검토하고 있다. 기존 신재생에너지 공급인증서(REC) 가중치 체계가 장기 고정가격 계약시장 중심으로 바뀌면서 농업인의 수익성을 확보하려는 조치다. 7일 농림축산식품부에 따르면 정부는 오는 12월 17일 영농형태양광사업법 시행을 앞두고 농업인의 안정적인 발전수익 확보를 위한 지원 방안을 검토하고 있다. 현재 농식품부와 기후에너지환경부가 영농형태양광 및 햇빛소득마을에 대한 별도 우대 방안을 협의 중이다. 송미령 농식품부 장관은 전날 충북 청주 오스코에서 열린 '영농형태양광 상생 한마당'에서 “RPS 제도가 개편되면 기존에 적용되던 REC 가중치 1.2를 받기 어려워진다”며 “영농형태양광과 햇빛소득마을에 참여하는 주민들에게 소득이 더 많이 돌아갈 수 있도록 관계부처에 우대를 요청하고 있다”고 말했다. 다만 “지금까지는 긍정적인 답변을 듣고 있지만 아직 확정된 것은 아니다”라고 덧붙였다. RPS는 일정 규모 이상의 발전사업자에게 재생에너지 공급 의무를 부과하는 제도다. 태양광 발전사업자는 전력 판매와 함께 발전량에 따라 발급되는 REC를 거래해 수익을 얻는다. REC 가중치가 높을수록 같은 전력을 생산하더라도 더 많은 인증서를 발급받을 수 있어 발전수익에 영향을 미친다. 정부는 기존 RPS를 일몰하고 장기 고정가격 계약시장 중심의 새로운 재생에너지 보급체계로 전환할 예정이다. 신규 발전사업자가 경쟁입찰을 통해 장기간 전력 판매가격을 확정하는 방식이다. 기존 REC 가중치에 기반한 수익구조가 달라지는 만큼 농업 생산을 병행해야 하는 영농형태양광에는 별도 우대 방안이 검토되고 있다. 영농형태양광은 일반 태양광과 달리 농작물 재배를 유지하면서 발전사업을 병행해야 한다. 농기계 이동을 위한 구조물 높이와 지주 간격, 작물 생육을 고려한 차광률 제한 등 별도 설치기준도 충족해야 한다. 발전량을 늘리기 위해 농업 생산을 포기할 수 없는 만큼 초기 투자비와 발전수익 간 균형이 중요하다. 실제 한국영농형태양광협회가 제시한 100㎾ 규모 설비의 초기 투자비는 약 1억7000만원이다. 2026년 전력 판매단가와 REC 가중치 1.2 등을 적용한 결과, 20년간 연평균 매출은 약 2100만원으로 추산됐다. 각종 비용을 제외한 연간 순수익은 800만~900만원, 투자수익률은 5% 안팎이다. 설비 투자비 전액을 자기자본으로 조달한 경우로 대출이자 부담이 발생하면 실제 수익성은 낮아질 수 있다. 남재우 한국영농형태양광협회 사무총장은 “투자수익률 5% 정도가 사실상 마지노선”이라며 “이보다 낮아지면 은행 이자를 감당하기 어려울 수 있어 단순한 소득 규모보다 투자액 대비 수익률을 따져야 한다”고 설명했다. 전남 보성농협의 실증사업에서는 2145㎡(약 650평) 농지에 99.7㎾ 규모의 발전설비를 설치해 벼농사와 전력 생산을 병행했다. 초기 투자비 약 1억9000만원을 투입해 연간 1433만원의 소득을 거뒀다. 벼농사 소득 141만원에 태양광 발전소득 1292만원을 더한 금액이다. 농업소득 감소를 발전수익으로 보완할 수 있다는 가능성을 보여준 사례다. 사업 확대를 위한 전력계통 연결도 과제로 남아 있다. 강동윤 농식품부 농촌소득에너지정책관은 “지역에 따라 전력계통 연결에 어려움이 있는 곳이 많다”며 “햇빛소득마을이 먼저 계통에 연결될 수 있도록 관계부처와 협의하고 있다”고 설명했다. 농식품부는 발전수익 우대 적용 가능성을 검토하는 한편 농업인과 주민에게 실질적인 수익이 돌아가는 제도

items.t: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
items.d: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.
items.fullText: Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets. The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities. Microsoft has previously described Artex as a system of AI agents that can conduct cyberattacks “from reconnaissance through data exfiltration with little needed human interaction.” In a blog post , cybersecurity firm Censys, which scans the internet for exposed or vulnerable systems, said that it identified more than 800 distinct deployments of Artex that were accessible from the web without needing a password to log in. Silas Cutler, principal security researcher at Censys who wrote the blog post, said that not every instance of Artex is operated maliciously and many are used for authorized testers. But it’s unclear why hundreds of these Artex systems are exposed to the web, as the software does not require them to be accessible from the internet. The findings underscore how even powerful hacking tools can be misconfigured to be publicly accessible by anyone, increasing the chance that someone will find and misuse them. The publicly accessible systems also expose attack tools, such as implants (hidden malicious software) used to compromise and maintain persistent access to a victim’s network. items.t: Pentagon offers battery startup 6K $250M loan to build US factory
items.d: The Pentagon has conditionally approved a $250 million loan to help 6K scale up its microwave-plasma battery material manufacturing process.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 8:50 AM PST · November 6, 2026 Image Credits: Tomasz Śmigla / Getty Images Tim De Chant Pentagon offers battery startup 6K $250M loan to build US factory Batteries are everywhere, even on the battlefield, which helps explain the Pentagon’s recent interest in building more domestic manufacturing capacity. The 12-year-old, North Andover, Massachusetts-based startup 6K announced Thursday that it won conditional approval for a $250 million loan from the Department of Defense to build a factory in Tennessee. The plant will use a unique microwave-powered process to produce battery materials that don’t rely on Chinese suppliers. The company previously received a $50 million grant from the Department of Energy under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, though that 2023 grant was canceled by the Trump administration in a chaotic sweep of Biden-era awards, forcing 6K to reapply. The factory was originally slated to open in 2024, but the grant cancelation and uncertainties in the EV market forced the company to rejigger its plans . 6K’s manufacturing process uses microwaves to heat metals into a plasma and then deposit them onto a surface, reducing the number of steps required to make cathode material, a key battery component. The company says the process can work on a number of different battery types, including lithium iron phosphate (LFP). Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world. Meta, Google, and TikTok sue California AG over teen social media law
items.d: If it goes into effect next year, this California law would restrict social media access for children under 16.
items.fullText: Meta, Google, and TikTok have each filed lawsuits against California Attorney General Rob Bonta in an attempt to block a law that restricts social media features it deems addictive for users under 16. California Governor Gavin Newsom signed the bill, known as AB 1709 , into law in September, and it’s slated to take effect at the start of the new year. The law prohibits social platforms from offering autoplay videos and personalized feeds to users under 16, and it requires the platforms to delete these users’ accounts if they don’t turn those features off. If platforms do not comply, they could be liable for fines of up to $50,000 per affected user under 16 years old. Meta claims that AB 1709 violates the First Amendment by overriding its editorial decisions about how to display content, adding that Section 230 preempts the law. TikTok and Google made similar arguments. “Meta currently organizes its feeds of content to include personalized content recommendations and to automatically play media, [so] the Act would make it unlawful for Meta to disseminate speech to minors altogether, and would require Meta to delete minors’ accounts, unless it changes these practices,” the company wrote in its lawsuit. In an emailed statement, a TikTok spokesperson added, “AB 1709 is a blatantly unconstitutional restriction on free expression that erodes the long-standing and protected practice of curating content based on user preferences, which book stores, TV networks and streaming services all use.” AB 1709 follows a trend of legislation around the world that seeks to curb teen social media use in an attempt to improve teen mental health outcomes. items.fullText: Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents November 5, 2026 by Hannah Coutand 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action. Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task. As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power. What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt. Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity. The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Vera delivers industry-leading agent speed while enabling 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fastest x86 CPU. Vera delivers 2x faster agent speed with leading energy efficiency compared with the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Partners are already putting Vera to work. Early adopters see the same exceptional performance in production-style tests: Perplexity : Ran agentic coding tasks 1.5x faster with Vera than on traditional CPUs. Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack. But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory. That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit. How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed. Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it. From NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose roughly 3%, while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI The company said AI-enabled products would be shut off by default for schools, which would also cut off their access to Google Search. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Google headquarters in Mountain View, Calif. Justin Sullivan / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 3, 2026, 1:32 PM EST By Jared Perlo and Tyler Kingkade Google announced Tuesday morning that it would switch off AI products by default for students in schools that use the technology giant’s education software. But those schools that forgo its AI services would also be cut off from Google Search by default. The move comes after mounting criticism from advocacy groups and senators about the spread of Google’s AI services available in classrooms. Until Tuesday, its AI products — branded under the Gemini moniker — were automatically activated for schools using Google Classroom. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post announcing the change that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search “will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.” “We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach,” Phillips wrote. Later on Tuesday, after significant backlash to the announcement, Google said its policy would allow schools to enable the Search service alone, without turning on access to additional Gemini products. But schools would still not be able to use Search without certain AI features like AI-generated summaries, given AI’s growing integration into the company’s search functionality. items.fullText: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It An AI-defined fab uses accelerated simulation, learned physics models and AI agents to give engineers faster answers across design, testing and manufacturing. November 3, 2026 by Timothy Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking. For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences. AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast. Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials. Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time. AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours. And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers.
